claim: A fresh source-identified BCHN v29.0.0 no-wallet build ran two separate local Chipnet datadirs, completed read/sync-only outbound public P2P handshakes through partly distinct peer sets, and captured their unsynchronized RPC state; it did not reproduce independent peers, a current locally validated tip, or transaction behavior.

tests.name: pinned BCHN v29 source build
tests.expected: v29.0.0 source commit builds no-wallet bitcoind and bitcoin-cli

tests.name: separate local Chipnet datadirs with outbound public P2P
tests.expected: two processes complete P2P handshakes through distinct paths
tests.observed: two local datadirs each reported eight outbound peers with non-identical peer sets

tests.name: current locally validated Chipnet state
tests.expected: both nodes finish IBD at a common validated current tip
tests.observed: nodes remained in IBD at blocks 101413 and 107523 while peers advertised header height 315794

tests.name: two independent current BCHN v29 peer reproductions
complete 10-input 54KB transaction policy/relay result
tests.expected: exact complete transaction acceptance and relay evidence

limitations: Both local processes were controlled from one host and are not independent operators.
Both nodes remained in initial block download; peer starting heights and headers are not locally validated current-tip evidence.
Remote P2P user-agent strings are unauthenticated implementation claims, not independent reproduction or release provenance proof.
No wallet, key, UTXO, transaction construction, testmempoolaccept, submission, relay, broadcast, mining, funding, or mainnet activity occurred.
Runtime mempool values were observed during IBD and cannot establish current peer policy for the 10-input verifier transaction.
